analysis:
Examined the ClusterService.swift head lines 911-1577 and the ClusterServiceControl.swift patch hunks.

Changed ranges in ClusterService.swift (head 99, 144-147, 164-168, 175, 337-420) fall in units outside this batch, except for the code around supervise. Lines 911-1577 are mostly unchanged context: status, checkForUpdate, checkApproval, supervise, partEnvironment and stopChild.

ClusterServiceControl changes:
(1) ensureControlResponder (head 109-119) now uses listenerChange/controlCheck instead of cableMove/controlCableCheck. It takes the selection from listenerSelection() rather than context.linkSelection(), and the port and policy from an injected `listening` value. The default is `Listening = .init`, truncated in the patch excerpt.
(2) ensureControl (head 176-182) now also drops a stale control node when node.localID differs from pairing.localMemberID. This is a stricter pairing-change invalidation, i.e. a hardening.

No regression is identified. The responder is still built with the pairing from pairingStore and the controlLabel epoch.

Open integration questions:
- Whether the `Listening` default policy and controlPort keep the prior authentication and bind restrictions. The Listening type, listenerSelection() and listenerChange() are not visible here.
- Whether the `responder` property, now internal rather than private (head line 99), is used only in tests.
- Whether a policy value could relax peer-pin checks on the control listener, which accepts lease and stop commands from the paired Mac.

The cluster pairing link is not modeled in the canonical threat model. It touches A-018 availability and T-041 via cache reclaim at head lines 1406-1409, which is unchanged.
